denomProfiles/stone-campbell-restoration: American movement to unite Christians by restoring New Testament Christianity.
"Where the Scriptures speak, we speak; where the Scriptures are silent, we are silent."
No creed but Christ: human creeds are rejected as tests of fellowship.
Faith, repentance and believer's immersion "for the remission of sins".
Christian unity through a return to the primitive church.
Weekly celebration of the Lord's Supper.
Congregational autonomy with elders and deacons.
Debates and periodicals, such as Campbell's Millennial Harbinger.
The a cappella wing, separately listed from 1906.
Leader of the "Christians" and of Cane Ridge.
Author of the Declaration and Address (1809).
Evangelist of the "five-finger exercise" of salvation.

Disciples missionaries worked in central India from 1882 (Harda, Jabalpur, Bilaspur); those churches joined the Church of North India in 1970, while later Churches of Christ missions planted congregations in southern India.
denomProfiles/seventh-day-adventist/tagl: Sabbath-keeping, health-minded church awaiting the soon return of Christ.
denomProfiles/seventh-day-adventist/core: The 28 Fundamental Beliefs, grounded in Scripture as the only rule of faith.
The seventh-day Sabbath (Saturday) as a perpetual sign of creation and redemption.
The imminent, visible Second Coming of Christ.
Christ's ministry in the heavenly sanctuary, including the investigative judgment begun in 1844.
Conditional immortality: the dead sleep until the resurrection.
The gift of prophecy manifested in the ministry of Ellen G. White.
denomProfiles/seventh-day-adventist/focu: Preparing the world for Christ's return (the "Three Angels' Messages" of Revelation 14).
Health and wholeness: vegetarian diet, abstinence from alcohol and tobacco.
Education and medical work, with one of the largest Protestant school systems.
denomProfiles/seventh-day-adventist/prac: Worship from Friday sunset to Saturday sunset.
Quarterly communion with foot-washing (the ordinance of humility).
Health institutions such as Loma Linda University.
denomProfiles/seventh-day-adventist/infl: Sabbatarian Adventists who rejected Ellen White's authority formed a parallel body.
John Harvey Kellogg's Battle Creek Sanitarium shaped modern diet and breakfast cereals.
A 1930s reform movement led by Victor Houteff.
denomProfiles/seventh-day-adventist/keyF: Baptist preacher of the 1844 Advent message.
Physician of the health reform movement.
denomProfiles/seventh-day-adventist/memb: Baptised members reported by the General Conference Office of Archives, Statistics and Research.
denomProfiles/seventh-day-adventist/inIn: Adventist work in India began in the 1890s; the Southern Asia Division has its headquarters in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, and runs many schools and hospitals, along with Spicer Adventist University in Pune.
denomProfiles/churches-of-christ/tagline: A cappella restorationist congregations seeking to be simply New Testament churches.
denomProfiles/churches-of-christ/coreDoc: Scripture alone, read through command, example and necessary inference.
Faith, repentance, confession and immersion for the remission of sins.
The church as the body of Christ, rather than a denomination.
Silence of Scripture as prohibitive: practices without New Testament warrant are not adopted.
denomProfiles/churches-of-christ/focuses: Restoring the pattern of the New Testament church.
Christian higher education (Abilene Christian, Harding, Pepperdine, Lipscomb).
denomProfiles/churches-of-christ/practic: Congregations led by elders (male) and served by deacons and evangelists.
No missionary societies or central headquarters; cooperation through sponsoring congregations.
denomProfiles/churches-of-christ/influen: The Boston movement (1979) grew out of Churches of Christ discipling ministries.
A 1950s division over congregational support of institutions.
denomProfiles/churches-of-christ/keyFigu: Leader of the Sand Creek Address (1889).
denomProfiles/churches-of-christ/inIndia: Churches of Christ have planted many congregations in India since the mid-twentieth century, especially in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Tamil Nadu, often through partnerships with American congregations.
denomProfiles/christian-church-disciples: Mainline restorationist church: "a movement for wholeness in a fragmented world".
Jesus Christ is Lord and Saviour; no creed beyond the confession of faith in Christ.
Freedom of belief and interpretation within a shared covenant.
Christian unity as God's will for the church.
The Lord's table open to all believers.
Ecumenism: a founding member of the World Council of Churches (1948).
Justice and anti-racism work.
Weekly communion as the centre of worship.
Partnership with the United Church of Christ (since 1989).
Weekly open communion, often presided over by lay elders.
Believer's baptism by immersion, while recognising other baptisms.
Congregational life within regional and general "manifestations" set up by the 1968 Restructure.
Ordination of women, since 1888.
Church of North India
Its Indian mission churches joined the 1970 union.
United Church of Christ
Full communion partner.
The Christian Century
Founded as a Disciples paper, it became the leading mainline magazine.
Alexander Campbell
Movement founder.
Barton W. Stone
Movement founder.
Charles Clayton Morrison
Editor of The Christian Century.
Sharon Watkins
First woman to lead a mainline US denomination (2005).
Disciples missions in central India, begun in 1882, became part of the Church of North India in 1970.
denomProfiles/christian-churches-churche: Independent instrumental congregations of the Restoration Movement, evangelical and non-denominational.
The Bible as the inspired authority; no creed but Christ.
Faith, repentance and baptism by immersion for the forgiveness of sins.
Congregational autonomy without a denominational headquarters.
Christian unity through restoring New Testament Christianity.
Evangelism and church growth, including several large megachurches.
Bible college and seminary training.
Mission work supported directly by congregations.
Restoration ideals combined with evangelical identity.
Weekly Lord's Supper.
Instrumental music in worship, unlike the a cappella Churches of Christ.
Elders and ministers, usually men.
Fellowship through the North American Christian Convention (founded 1927).
Evangelical megachurches
Congregations such as Southeast Christian Church (Louisville) became influential models.
Bible college movement
Schools such as Cincinnati Bible Seminary trained ministers across the movement.
P. H. Welshimer
Pastor of First Christian Church, Canton, Ohio.
Edwin R. Errett
Editor of the Christian Standard.
Bob Russell
Founding pastor of Southeast Christian Church.
denomProfiles/community-of-christ/taglin: Former RLDS Church: a Latter Day Saint tradition now focused on peace and justice.
denomProfiles/community-of-christ/coreDo: God as Trinity, affirmed in its Basic Beliefs.
Continuing revelation through a prophet-president, recorded in its Doctrine and Covenants.
The Bible as the foundational scripture, with the Book of Mormon used as additional scripture.
Worth of all persons and the pursuit of peace (Zion) on earth.
denomProfiles/community-of-christ/focuse: Peace, reconciliation and healing of the spirit.
Justice for the poor and marginalised.
The Temple in Independence, Missouri (dedicated 1994), devoted to peace.
Inclusive community, including LGBTQ members in many nations.
denomProfiles/community-of-christ/practi: Eight sacraments: baptism (from age eight), confirmation, Lord's Supper, marriage, blessing of children, laying on of hands for the sick, ordination and evangelist blessing.
A daily Prayer for Peace at the Temple.
denomProfiles/community-of-christ/influe: Members who rejected women's ordination formed independent branches after 1984.
denomProfiles/community-of-christ/keyFig: Founding prophet of the Latter Day Saint movement.
First president not descended from Joseph Smith (1996).
denomProfiles/church-of-god-seventh-day/: Sabbath-keeping Adventists who rejected Ellen White's visions.
The seventh-day Sabbath as binding on Christians.
Scripture alone, without a modern prophet's authority.
Conditional immortality: the dead sleep until the resurrection.
A historically non-Trinitarian view of God, with Father and Son distinct and the Spirit as God's power.
Prophetic teaching about the last days.
Publishing, such as the Bible Advocate (from 1863).
An annual Lord's Supper on the evening of Passover, with foot-washing.
Herbert W. Armstrong was a Church of God (Seventh Day) minister before founding his own movement.
Some offshoots adopted Hebrew names for God.
Former minister who founded the Radio Church of God.
denomProfiles/pentecostal/tagline: Global renewal movement of Spirit baptism, tongues, healing and fervent mission.
denomProfiles/pentecostal/coreDoctrines/: Baptism in the Holy Spirit as an experience after conversion.
Speaking in tongues as the initial physical evidence (in classical Pentecostalism).
The "full gospel": Jesus as Saviour, Baptiser in the Spirit, Healer and Coming King.
Divine healing provided in the atonement.
The imminent, premillennial return of Christ.
denomProfiles/pentecostal/practices/0: Spontaneous worship with tongues, prophecy and prayer for the sick.
denomProfiles/pentecostal/practices/2: Altar calls and tarrying for the Spirit.
denomProfiles/pentecostal/practices/3: Lay and women's ministry from the earliest revivals.
denomProfiles/pentecostal/influenced/2/t: Pentecostal spirituality entered the historic churches from 1960.
denomProfiles/pentecostal/keyFigures/1/r: Leader of the Azusa Street revival (1906).
denomProfiles/pentecostal/keyFigures/2/r: First to speak in tongues at Topeka (1901).
denomProfiles/pentecostal/keyFigures/3/r: Leader of the Mukti revival in India (1905).
denomProfiles/pentecostal/members/note: Pew Research Center (2011) estimate of Pentecostal Christians worldwide, excluding charismatics.
denomProfiles/pentecostal/inIndia: Pentecostal experience appeared in the 1905–07 Mukti revival; Indian churches such as the Indian Pentecostal Church of God (1924) and The Pentecostal Mission, together with the Assemblies of God, are strongest in Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.
denomProfiles/assemblies-of-god/tagline: The largest Pentecostal fellowship, founded at Hot Springs, Arkansas, in 1914.
denomProfiles/assemblies-of-god/coreDoct: The Statement of Fundamental Truths (1916), including the Trinity against Oneness teaching.
Baptism in the Holy Spirit with tongues as the initial physical evidence.
Divine healing as provided in the atonement.
Salvation by grace through faith, with progressive sanctification ("finished work").
The pre-tribulation rapture and premillennial reign of Christ.
denomProfiles/assemblies-of-god/focuses/: World missions and indigenous church planting (self-governing, self-supporting, self-propagating).
denomProfiles/assemblies-of-god/practice: Believer's baptism by immersion and the Lord's Supper as ordinances.
Expressive worship with tongues, interpretation and prophecy.
Cooperative fellowship mixing congregational and presbyterian structures.
Ordination of women as ministers, since 1935.
denomProfiles/assemblies-of-god/influenc: David Yonggi Cho's Seoul church belongs to the Korean Assemblies of God.
Affiliated with the World Assemblies of God Fellowship.
Its missions planted national churches on every continent.
denomProfiles/assemblies-of-god/members/: Adherents of member churches of the World Assemblies of God Fellowship, as reported by the Fellowship.
denomProfiles/assemblies-of-god/inIndia: Assemblies of God missionaries worked in India from the 1910s; today Assemblies of God churches are found nationwide, notably in Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Kolkata, where Mark Buntain built a church, school and hospital from 1954.
